definition: A period of fifteen days; in older ecclesiastical or legal use, the fifteenth day after a feast or event.
etymology: It came into Middle English through Anglo-French quinzine, a word built on quinze, “fifteen.” The word kept the count even as its spelling shifted into English.
usage: September 15, the month’s midpoint, makes a fitting marker for a quindene: one fifteen-day stretch has quietly run its course.
